newsitem.title: INDIA: Polling begins in India's Punjab elections.
newsitem.headline: Polling begins in India's Punjab elections.

text.p: Polls opened in India's northern state of Punjab on Friday under tight security for the election of a new local government, officials said.
Polling stations opened at 7.30 a.m. (0200 GMT) in Punjab and are scheduled to close at 4.30 p.m. (1100 GMT). Around 15.2 million voters were eligible to vote, officials said.
The election to the 117-seat state assembly will be the first local poll in two decades not overshadowed by Sikh separatist violence in which more than 20,000 people died.
State polls in 1992, which revived local democracy after more than a decade of separatist violence, were held amid fears and overbearing security.
India has poured in 100,000 paramilitary soldiers to oversee elections.
The counting of ballots is expected to start on Sunday and results are likely to announced on the same day, officials said.
